lateral_flank_blob_constellation.centroid_triangulation: A semi-regular grid of high-luminance circular clusters is visible posterior to the branchial region. Larger, higher-intensity blobs are arranged in approximately four identifiable horizontal rows along the mid-lateral flank, with density increasing and spot size decreasing toward the posterior-dorsal region.
lateral_flank_blob_constellation.stripe_intersections: Faint vertical bands of elevated pixel intensity intersect with horizontal carinae to form anchor nodes for the primary high-luminance blobs, creating a rectangular lattice pattern most visible in the mid-flank section.

carinae_gradient_vectors.ridge_trajectory: Three distinct horizontal ridges are visible running along the upper third of the flank. These features are defined by a sharp intensity gradient, with high-luminance values on the dorsal-facing edge and significant shadowing on the ventral-facing edge.

dorsal_fin_surface_patterning.internal_spot_density: The visible first dorsal fin contains a high density of small, high-luminance blobs distributed uniformly across the visible surface, appearing smaller and more compact than the spots on the primary lateral flank.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Multiple prominent white linear features are visible on the lower-left flank. Two long, parallel, slightly curved white lines run horizontally across the mid-lateral region, consistent with deep tissue scarring or mechanical trauma. Additional shorter, irregular white markings are visible further posterior.
other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced light-refraction caustics (dancing light patterns) are projected onto the lower-left portion of the shark's flank, partially obscuring the underlying pigmentation and scars.
